INES (CONT'D) / We both know it isn't my name you want. So. What's it worth to you. / Rafael's stick goes still. Outside, the rain has not stopped, and ahead of them Alentejo is still just a word the night hasn't reached.
What do you want, Sombra. / RAFAEL / A name on a page. Whose hand pulled the fishplates at Vale de Figueira — written in hers, not in mine.
RAFAEL / Somebody told him more than that. / He leans forward, takes the blind by its cord, and pulls it down over the glass.
Of course there is. / RAFAEL / The report wasn’t signed by a junior inspector. It was signed by me.

“His.” / A pause on the line, long enough that the pips start. / “Then it was yours the moment you taught him,” Sister Benedict says. “Bring me the form at six. And Alma — don’t let him count again tonight.”

“Then I’ll stay on nights.” / The paper in Alma’s pocket has a corner sharper than paper should be. She feels it against her thumb, once, and takes her hand out. / “No, you won’t,” she says. “You’ll do something for me first.”

He reads it. He reads it again. The name box in the ledger, filled in — he thinks of the book under his arm and cannot make his hand go for it. / Under his fingertips the pulse changes. Not a jump, not a stumble. It climbs, steady and unhurried, one beat at a
The sheet is not flat. It has the shape of a person in it. / Alma looks at the wrist on the pillow. The band is warm. It says REYES, A. NINE. / She looks at her own wrist. It's bare.

ACT THREE / Muster at six. Four volunteers, cold hands around mugs, rain on the roof like gravel. / “Overnight log,” Mara says. “Two-forty. We took a weak transmission. Garbled. No station ID. No response to challenge.

“There’s a thing I’m obliged to raise,” he says. “Coastguard logger’s got a transmission off this desk at two-forty-one. Thirty-eight seconds on sixteen. That’s a distress acknowledgement, and it isn’t in your logbook, and it isn’t on your tape.” / Theo’s arms
"Say it again," Theo says. "Say it again." / Hiss. / He turns the notebook round, runs his finger down the copied roster. "Who's after Rusk on this?"
The heater ticks. Theo writes it down. / "Say it again," Mara says, to the speaker, to the erased tape, to the rain. "Say it—" / Hiss.

"Six o'clock," she says. "I'll want you at this desk, Chief. Whether you believe it or you don't." / He picks up his cap. "And if I'm not here?" / Theo re-threads the tape. "Then you'll be at the bearing."
